Outbound calls (`run: api`, `run: webhook`): how URL values are encoded and who may choose the host, redirects, 4xx handling, timeouts and what a failed call stops.

**`run: api` URL values are encoded for where they land.** A `:param` or `{{ref}}` in the path is path-escaped (`/`, `?`, `#` become data; a value of only dots is refused), in the query or fragment it is query-escaped, and in the host only host characters are accepted. A `{{env.X}}` value and a ref at the very start of the URL stay verbatim (a configured base URL, a stored `next` link). Request input may not choose the scheme or host of a call that carries an auth header, a signer, any env value, or a header other than a literal Content-Type, Accept, Accept-Language or User-Agent, nor of a call that sends a value an earlier step derived from env (a SQL param, `run: set` value, loop row, `enqueue` payload or authenticated api response built from `${{ env.X }}`); for that last kind a URL at the very start that the producing step fixed itself still works: a quoted literal of that step (a token endpoint picked with `CASE ... THEN 'https://...' END` in the step that also reads the request) or exactly an env value it reads (`:base AS url` with `base: ${{ env.APP_BASE_URL }}`), but not text joined onto either. So split a value like `owner/repo` into two refs (`/repos/{{owner}}/{{repo}}`), and pass a whole query string through `with.query:` instead of splicing it into the URL. Form bodies (`with.form`) are form-encoded, so a value containing `&` or `=` stays one value. The same encoding applies to `run: webhook` URLs. A `run: webhook` with no `body:` (or one that renders empty) posts the whole flow context, so when its URL reads request input or a data-event row column the step fails instead: write the `body:` it should send. The one exception is a caller who is the app's global admin acting as itself, by session or API token (a service account asking for a delivery callback): it keeps the whole-context post. A whole-context post never carries a value derived from env, whatever the URL: a key a step built from `${{ env.X }}` (a `run: set` value, a SQL step or api call that read one, a loop row over one) is left out with its dotted keys, and so is any string that holds an env value or such a derived value (a stored row echoing a key). To send one, name it in `body:` or `payload:`. A step with `payload:` sends that payload and never the context. A request flow's `run: api` whose scheme or host comes from `${{ params.X }}` while the call carries credentials (any of the above) is refused when written and by benmore check, and the runtime refuses every such call. A signed-in caller's profile value is request input here too: `https://${{ user.last_name }}/...` with an env header would let the caller pick the host that receives the secret by editing their last name, so it is refused like `params.X`, also when routed through a set or step output, and only the framework's account columns (user.id, user.email, user.role, ...) stay trusted (api({at:'flows'}) → identity_binding).

Outbound redirects: a same-origin redirect keeps every header; a cross-origin redirect keeps only Accept, Accept-Language and User-Agent (auth, API-key and signer headers are dropped), and a cross-origin redirect of a non-GET request fails the step. Outbound calls ignore HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY. A method-override header (`X-HTTP-Method-Override`, `X-HTTP-Method`, `X-Method-Override`) must be a literal or env value: request input there, in `headers:` or in a `sign:` binding that sets one, fails the step (the method is the one in `method:`).

`run: api` treats HTTP 4xx as errors unless `with.handled_statuses: [400]` explicitly lists one or more integer 400–499 codes. Listed responses are captured in the usual status/body/headers/json envelope and still pass through `success_when`; malformed, duplicate, non-4xx, or paginated combinations are rejected. 5xx, transport/read failures and responses over 1 MiB remain errors.

**api steps honor `timeout:`.** `with: { timeout: 570s }` (or a bare number = seconds, or step-level `timeout:` which wins) caps the outbound call; the default is 30s. A synchronous flow also ends at its own time limit (30 s by default, `on.request.timeout` up to 95 s; see time_limits), where the call is cut whatever the step's timeout says, so a longer call needs `mode: async` on on.request.

**Outbound failures stop before success.** An api or webhook step with an unresolved value in its URL, query, body, auth, headers or signer bindings fails before signing/token exchange or delivery; use an explicit default for optional inputs. A webhook succeeds only on a final 2xx response; other statuses fail the step, so later success steps do not run. External effects from earlier steps are not rolled back. Respond bodies written as arrays resolve nested references and preserve native types like object bodies; a missing value returns template_unresolved before the success response is written.
